Definition: from G4253 and G138; to choose for oneself before another thing (prefer), i.e. (by implication) to propose (intend):--purpose.
BiblicalUsage: Proaireomai means to choose beforehand, to purpose in advance. Paul uses it once, for giving: every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loveth a cheerful giver.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that giving decided in advance is giving done in freedom, and cheerfulness is the proof the heart chose it.
